title: Entra ID Sign-In Anomalies

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `mscs:azure:signinlog` events with `riskLevelDuringSignIn!="none"` into `index=azure`. Confirm UC-4.2.2 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `mscs:azure:signinlog` traffic without `riskLevelDuringSignIn!="none"`. Confirm UC-4.2.2 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=azure` sourcetype=`mscs:azure:signinlog` collected via `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=azure sourcetype="mscs:azure:signinlog" riskLevelDuringSignIn!="none"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.2.2_entra_id_sign_in_anomali_2"
| sort -_time
description: UC-4.2.2 — Entra ID Sign-In Anomalies: queries Microsoft Azure `mscs:azure:signinlog` for search criteria `riskLevelDuringSignIn!="none"` and returns actor, resource, and region context for security review and change validation.
value: On Microsoft Azure, detecting 'Entra ID Sign-In Anomalies' early shortens cloud incident response and produces defensible audit evidence for identity and change-management controls. UC-4.2.2 drives critical-priority security alerting before customer-impacting drift.
implementation: Forward Entra ID sign-in logs via Event Hub or direct API. Alert on riskLevelDuringSignIn = high or medium. Correlate with conditional access policy results.
visualization: Table (user, risk level, location, IP), Map (sign-in locations), Timeline, Bar chart by risk type.
cimSpl:
| tstats `summariesonly` count
  from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication
  by Authentication.user Authentication.action Authentication.src span=1h
| sort -count
dataModelAcceleration: Enable data model acceleration for Authentication (Authentication dataset).
knownFalsePositives: Some risky scores come from new devices, working from home, or a partner logging in the same way we do. We do not want every medium flag to page us; we pair higher scores with new locations, odd hours, or multiple clouds before we act.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=azure`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` with the modular input for `mscs:azure:signinlog`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.2.58.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Forward Entra ID sign-in logs via Event Hub or direct API. Alert on riskLevelDuringSignIn = high or medium. Correlate with conditional access policy results.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=azure sourcetype="mscs:azure:signinlog" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=azure sourcetype="mscs:azure:signinlog" riskLevelDuringSignIn!="none"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.2.2_entra_id_sign_in_anomali_2"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `mscs:azure:signinlog` in `index=azure` to detect entra id sign-in anomalies. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_2_2_alert` with severity aligned to `critical` criticality. Dashboard: Table (user, risk level, location, IP), Map (sign-in locations), Timeline, Bar chart by risk type..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of entra id sign-in anomalies so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
